verses.summary: Jacob predicts Joseph's election and teaching of dream interpretation; ancestral Abraham/Isaac blessing motifs may offer contextual comparison but no precise earlier wording checked.
Introductory claim that Joseph and his brothers contain signs for questioners; no source-specific earlier parallel established.

Brothers complain that Joseph and his brother are more loved by their father; Genesis 37:3–4 describes Jacob's special love for Joseph and the brothers' hatred, but not the same reference to Joseph's brother.

Brothers propose killing Joseph or casting him into a distant land, hoping for their father's exclusive attention and later righteousness; Genesis 37:18–20 describes plotting to kill Joseph, with distinct motivation and outcome.

One brother counsels against killing Joseph and proposes throwing him into a well to be picked up by travelers; Genesis 37:21–24 attributes a rescue intervention to Reuben and places Joseph in a pit; subsequent sale differs in narrative sequence.

candidates.similarity: Paternal preference for Joseph and resulting brotherly hostility.
candidates.difference: Qur'an mentions Joseph and his brother and a complaint of parental error; Genesis foregrounds Joseph's special garment and the brothers' hatred.

candidates.difference: Qur'an mentions removal to another land and subsequent moral reform; Genesis frames conspiracy in relation to dreams.

candidates.similarity: A brother opposes murder and suggests placing Joseph in a pit.
candidates.difference: Qur'an has an unnamed speaker and travelers who might retrieve him; Genesis names Reuben and describes his intention to rescue Joseph.
candidates.verification_needed: Check Hebrew/Greek/Syriac witnesses and differences in well/pit vocabulary.

dossier.title: Joseph, his brothers and the pit: Qur'an 12:8–10 and Genesis 37
dossier.background: Genesis 37 narrates Jacob's favoritism and the brothers' conspiracy; Qur'an 12 reorganizes the scene with a brotherly debate and a plan involving a well and passing travelers.
dossier.similarities: Favoritism, sibling jealousy, a contemplated killing and an alternative involving a pit.
dossier.differences: Genesis names Reuben and describes a special garment; Qur'an leaves the objecting brother unnamed and gives the travelers a role in the proposal.
dossier.variant_witnesses: Hebrew MT, Greek Septuagint and Syriac Peshitta require passage-specific collation; no claim made about the survival of any particular ancient fragment.
dossier.dating: Genesis textual traditions predate the Qur'an; date of composition/redaction is distinct from dates of extant manuscript witnesses. Precise witnesses not verified in this pass.
dossier.interpretations: A shared Joseph story complex is evident, but transmission pathways and dependence are not established by narrative resemblance.
